title: Dopant Ionization Fraction vs. Temperature
description: Interactive plot of the fraction of ionized donors or acceptors in silicon from 50 K to 600 K, with a band diagram showing how the Fermi level moves relative to the dopant level. The charge-neutrality equation is solved for the Fermi level at every temperature for a chosen dopant and doping concentration.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics

educational.topic: Ionization of donors and acceptors in silicon versus temperature
learningObjectives: Explain why shallow dopants are nearly fully ionized at 300 K
Predict the ionized fraction for a given dopant, doping concentration, and temperature
Identify when the complete-ionization approximation breaks down
prerequisites: Fermi-Dirac statistics and effective density of states

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with real-time plots and a probe-temperature readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the ionized fraction before moving the temperature or doping slider, then check the readout
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the ionized fraction of indium at 300 K
Explain why heavier doping lowers the ionized fraction
Find the temperature at which 90 percent of the dopants are ionized

simulationModel.modelType: physics-based, numerical solution of charge neutrality
equations: n = Nc exp(-(Ec - Ef)/kT), p = Nv exp(-(Ef - Ev)/kT)
assumptions: Silicon with a single dopant species and no compensation
Nc = 2.86e19 and Nv = 3.10e19 cm^-3 at 300 K, scaled as T^1.5
Eg(0) set to 1.175 eV so that ni(300 K) = 9.65e9 cm^-3
limitations: Isolated dopant levels: the model underestimates ionization above about 1e18 cm^-3, so the doping slider stops there
Excited dopant states and temperature-dependent ionization energies are ignored
